en.title: Synchronous Eight-Neighbor Infection Until Stable
en.description:
At the end of each day, a healthy cell . becomes X if it had at least T infected neighbors X at the start of that day. Neighbors include up, down, left, right, and the four diagonals, 8 directions in total. Infected cells never recover. Return the last day on which a new infection occurs; if the grid is already stable initially, return 0. A check day with no change is not counted.

The input and output were compiled by this site.
en.input: The first line contains n m, the second line contains T, followed by n lines of m consecutive characters. 1≤n,m≤200, 0≤T≤8. Each character is X or .
en.output: A single non-negative integer, the number of rounds in which new infections occur.
en.explanation: In Example 1 the center infection spreads to all non-immune neighboring cells at once, so the answer is 1. In Example 2 there is only 1 infected neighbor while the threshold is 2, so the answer is 0. In Example 3 the threshold is 0, so no infection source is needed, and every healthy cell is infected on day 1.
hints: Maintain the number of infected neighbors of each cell. First find the cells that become infected on day 1, then process the queue of new infections layer by layer: each newly infected cell notifies only its at most 8 neighbors, and the next layer is processed on the following day. When T=0, all healthy cells enter layer 1.
